svg.text: The same picture, flat and bent
FPGA looks up the bitmap pixel
it came from (A) and copies it.
Nothing is left out or doubled.
A' is near a corner, so A lies
B' is near the middle, so B lies
the same picture, bent like a CRT:
edge middles stay put, corners pull in,
the monitor frame fills the rest
A screen pixel at distance r from the middle reads the bitmap at r times this factor, in the same direction.
distance r from the middle (1 = middle of an edge)
blue reads nearer in, amber further out,
grey reads past the bitmap: black
What the FPGA does for every pixel, 75 million times a second
No square root and no division: only multiplications, shifts and adds, in a pipeline 12 stages deep.
The result says which two bitmap pixels to read and how to blend them (see the ring buffer).
